newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-UNINSPIRED DUTCH BEAT SAN MARINO 4-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNINSPIRED DUTCH BEAT SAN MARINO 4-0.

text.p: The Netherlands, favourites to qualify for the World Cup finals from European group seven, needed two late goals to bring respectability to a 4-0 scoreline against the part-timers of San Marino on Saturday.

San Marino held the game scoreless up to a minute before half-time, largely through their favoured tactic of getting the whole team behind the ball in defence, until goalkeeper Federico Gasperoni let a Patrick Kluivert shot bobble through his legs.
The Dutch were unable to find a rhythm in their constant attacks, and poor touches and finishing in front of goal saw a number of clearcut chances go begging.

Frank de Boer scored in the 58th minute to silence the increasingly-disenchanted home fans, before a late header from substitute Pierre van Hooijdonk and a neat chip on the final whistle for De Boer's second added some gloss.

The Dutch captain, an unlikely top scorer from the centre of defence, said it had not been a pleasant night for his team, who now top their group with 12 points from four games, ahead of Belgium who have nine.
"It's not much fun playing against a team that just sit back," he said. "I don't think we really played that badly, but the chances we got just didn't go in."
Dennis Bergkamp was unable to make any more progress towards the Netherlands' scoring record on a night the Arsenal attacker looked out of touch.
He went clear through in the 88th minute after beating the offside trap, but shot straight at Gasperoni from point-blank range.

The San Marino keeper saved well from Kluivert and Clarence Seedorf early on, but was left stranded by a cross in the 82nd minute, allowing Van Hooijdonk to get behind him and nod into an empty net for the third goal.
De Boer put his vaunted strikeforce in the shade in extra time, carrying the ball forward from the edge of the area and neatly lifting it over the advancing goalkeeper for the fourth.
